userStories.title: The decisions sidecar module
acceptanceCriteria: `parseDecisionEntries([{ id: "B1", kind: "finding", disposition: "fixed", reason: "retry path fixed", sha: "a1b2c3d" }])` returns that one entry unchanged.
`parseDecisionEntries({ decisions: [] })` throws a `NaxError` with code `WORKFLOW_DECISIONS_INVALID` and message `decisions must be a JSON array`.
`parseDecisionEntries` on an entry whose `id` is `""` throws with message `decision 1: id must be a non-empty string`.
`parseDecisionEntries` on an entry `B1` whose `disposition` is `"accepted"` throws with message `decision B1: disposition must be one of fixed, waived, confirmed, overridden, verified`.
`parseDecisionEntries` on a `fixed` entry `B1` with no `sha` throws with message `decision B1: disposition fixed requires a sha`.
`parseDecisionEntries` on a `waived` entry `B1` carrying `sha` `a1b2c3d` throws with message `decision B1: sha is only allowed when disposition is fixed`.
`parseDecisionEntries` on an entry `B1` with `sha` `"xyz"` throws with message `decision B1: sha must be 7 to 40 hex characters`.
`parseDecisionEntries` on an entry `B1` whose `reason` is `"line one\nline two"` throws with message `decision B1: reason must be one non-empty line`.
`parseDecisionEntries` on an entry `B1` whose `reason` is `"   "` throws with message `decision B1: reason must be one non-empty line`.
`parseDecisionEntries` on two entries that both have `id` `B1` throws with message `decision B1 appears twice`.
`parseDecisionEntries` on an entry `B1` with `kind` `"bug"` throws with message `decision B1: kind must be one of finding, advisor, gate, ci, story, cannot-verify, minor, reason`.
`sidecarKindFor` returns `"advisor"` for an open item of kind `ruling` and `"finding"` for an open item of kind `finding`.
`checkEntriesAgainstItems` on an entry `B9` of kind `finding` and open items `B1` and `B2` throws with message `unknown item B9; open items: B1, B2`.
`checkEntriesAgainstItems` on an entry `B9` of kind `finding` and no open items throws with message `unknown item B9; open items: none`.
`checkEntriesAgainstItems` accepts an entry of kind `ci` with id `check:e2e` and an entry of kind `minor` with id `m1`, neither of which names an open item.
`checkEntriesAgainstItems` on an entry `B1` of kind `advisor` and an open item `B1` of kind `finding` throws with message `decision B1 has kind advisor but the open item is finding`.
`mergeDecisions` on existing entries `B1`, `B2` and an incoming entry `B2` with a new reason plus an entry `B3` returns `B1`, the new `B2`, then `B3`, in that order.
`sidecarFileName(new Date("2026-10-13T09:12:00.417Z"))` returns `decisions-2026-10-13T09-12-00-417Z.json`.

`newestSidecar` on a directory holding `decisions-2026-10-13T09-12-00-000Z.json`, `decisions-2026-10-14T10-00-00-000Z.json` and `result.json` returns the second file's path and parsed contents, and returns `null` for a directory with no `decisions-*.json` file.

After `writeSidecar(path, sidecar)`, `newestSidecar` on that directory returns `{ path, sidecar }` where `path` is the written path and `sidecar` equals the one written, and the directory holds no file other than the sidecar and those that were there before.

routing.reasoning: Single new pure-ish module with validation rules and atomic file write; standard patterns, clear messages in ACs.

userStories.title: nax workflow record
acceptanceCriteria: `readPrState("github", "https://gh/pr/7", deps, cwd)` runs `gh pr view https://gh/pr/7 --json isDraft,body,url` and, for stdout `{"isDraft":true,"body":"B","url":"https://gh/pr/7"}`, returns `{ isDraft: true, body: "B", url: "https://gh/pr/7" }`.

`readPrState("gitlab", "7", deps, cwd)` on stdout `{"draft":true,"description":"D","web_url":"https://gl/mr/7"}` returns `isDraft` true, `body` `"D"` and `url` `"https://gl/mr/7"`, and on `{"work_in_progress":true}` returns `isDraft` true.
`readPrState` on a forge command that exits 1 with stderr `not found` throws a `NaxError` with code `WORKFLOW_PR_READ_FAILED` and message `cannot read PR https://gh/pr/7: not found`.
`readPrState` on stdout that is not JSON throws a `NaxError` with code `WORKFLOW_PR_READ_FAILED`.

`workflow record -f auth --decisions d.json --json -d <dir>`, where the run has open item `B1` of kind `finding` and `d.json` holds one `fixed` entry for `B1` with sha `a1b2c3d`, creates exactly one `decisions-*.json` file in the run directory whose `artifact` is `<runId>/result.json`, `feature` is `auth`, `outcome` is `pending`, `decisions` equals the file's entries and `reasons` equals the record's `reasons`.

That call exits 0 and prints one JSON object whose `feature` is `auth`, `runId` is the run directory's name, `sidecar` is the sidecar's path relative to `<dir>`, `outcome` is `pending`, `decisions` is 1 and `unruled` is `[]`.
With open items `B1` and `B2` and a decisions file ruling only `B1`, the printed `unruled` is `["B2"]` and the exit code is 0.

A second `workflow record` call with a decisions file holding an entry for `B2`, after the first created the sidecar, leaves exactly one `decisions-*.json` file in the run directory and its `decisions` holds the entries for `B1` then `B2`.
A second call whose decisions file re-rules `B1` as `waived` with a new reason replaces the `B1` entry in the same sidecar and keeps its position.
`workflow record -f auth --outcome abandoned` with an existing sidecar rewrites that sidecar's `outcome` to `abandoned` and leaves its `decisions` unchanged.
`workflow record -f auth --outcome abandoned` on a run with no sidecar exits 1 with error `no decisions sidecar for run <runId>; pass --decisions` and creates no file.
`workflow record -f auth` with neither `--decisions` nor `--outcome` exits 1 with error `nothing to record: pass --decisions or --outcome`.
`workflow record -f auth --outcome done` exits 1 with error `outcome must be one of pending, promoted, verified-ready, abandoned` and reads no run directory.

`workflow record -f auth --outcome promoted` with an existing sidecar, where the stubbed forge's `pr view` call reports `isDraft` true, exits 1 with error `cannot record outcome promoted: PR is still a draft` and leaves the sidecar's bytes unchanged.
`workflow record -f auth --outcome promoted` with an existing sidecar, where the forge reports the PR as ready, sets the sidecar's `outcome` to `promoted` and its `url` to the record's `url`.
`workflow record -f auth --outcome verified-ready` where the forge reports the PR as a draft exits 1 with error `cannot record outcome verified-ready: PR is still a draft`.
`workflow record -f auth --outcome promoted` on a run whose record has no `url` exits 1 with error `cannot record outcome promoted: the workflow result has no PR url`.
A decisions file holding an entry for id `B9` of kind `finding`, with open items `B1` only, exits 1 with error `unknown item B9; open items: B1` and creates no sidecar.
A decisions file whose content is not JSON exits 1 with error `decisions file is not valid JSON: <path>`, and a path that does not exist exits 1 with error `cannot read decisions file: <path>`.
`workflow record -f ../x --decisions d.json` exits 1 with error `Feature name must be a single path segment: ../x` and reads no file.

`workflow record -f auth --decisions d.json` without `--json` prints `auth: recorded 1 decision(s) in <relative sidecar path>; outcome pending` and, when an open item is unruled, a second line `unruled: B2`.
`registerWorkflowCommand(new Command())` returns a group named `workflow` whose subcommand names equal `["status", "record"]`.
`workflow record -f auth --outcome promoted` when no forge is detected exits 1 with error `no forge detected for <dir>`.
`workflow record -f auth --decisions d.json` where the run has no readable `result.json` exits 1 with error `no workflow result for feature auth`.

userStories.title: nax workflow promote: validation and the dry run
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add `nax workflow promote -f <feature> [--yes] [--json]` with its validation steps, the `items-ruled` and `ci-green` checks and the report, performing no forge write.

**Motivation** — Promotion mechanics such as requiring checks green on the pushed head and never promoting a conflicting PR are rules an agent re-derives on every run, with the forge CLIs' argv written out by hand.

**Approach** — Add `waitForChecks: typeof waitForChecks` to `WorkflowForgeDeps` (the real `_workflowForgeDeps` uses `waitForChecks` from `src/workflow/ci-wait.ts`). Create `src/cli/workflow-promote.ts`; register `promote` (with its `--yes` flag) in `registerWorkflowCommand` after `record`; export its symbols from `src/cli/index.ts`. This story performs no forge write: with every check passing it prints the dry-run result whether or not `--yes` was given, and US-005, which lands in the same PR, adds the writes. IMPORT RULE: HEAD is read through `forgeDeps.forge.run(["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"], { cwd: dir })`, not through `readHead` (`src/workflow/git.ts` imports `step-context`, which imports `@/cli`, so a value import of it from `src/cli` closes a runtime import cycle). `workflow-promote.ts` imports workflow leaves by relative path and `src/cli/workflow.ts` only by `import type`; `bun run check:import-cycles` must stay clean.

```
nax workflow promote -f <feature> [--yes] [-d, --dir <path>] [--json]
```
`--dir` defaults to `process.cwd()` and is the project directory. `--json` prints exactly one JSON object on stdout; on an error it prints `{"error":"<message>"}` on stdout, and without `--json` the message goes to stderr through `deps.logErr` (the `status` convention).

Validation order: (1) the feature name; (2) `loadRunVerdict`; (3) the record's `outcome` is `draft`, else `workflow for <feature> ended <outcome or "not published">; only a draft can be promoted`; (4) the record has a `url`, else `the workflow result has no PR url`; (5) a forge is detected (`no forge detected for <dir>`); (6) `readPrState` reports the PR as a draft, else `PR is already ready: <url>`. Each failure exits `1` and writes nothing. Then both checks run, never short-circuiting each other:

- `items-ruled`: passes when every open item id has an entry in the newest sidecar of the run (vacuously when there are no open items). Otherwise `detail` is `no ruling recorded for <ids joined by ", ">`, and when the run has no sidecar at all, `no decisions recorded; run nax workflow record`.
- `ci-green`: `forgeDeps.waitForChecks(forge, url, { cwd: dir, timeoutMs: 0, pollMs: 0, expectedSha })`, where `expectedSha` is the trimmed stdout of `forgeDeps.forge.run(["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"], { cwd: dir })`; a non-zero exit fails the command with `cannot read HEAD: <stderr or exit code>`. It passes only for outcome `green`; `no-checks`, `pending`, `unavailable`, `failed` and `conflicting` all fail, with `detail` `ci <outcome>: <the result's detail>`.

Without `--yes`, or with any check failed, no forge write happens. Exit `0` when both checks pass (the dry run reports `dryRun: true, promoted: false` and the line `ready to promote; rerun with --yes`), `2` when any check failed.

Plain output of promote: one line per check (`pass  items-ruled` / `FAIL  ci-green  <detail>`), then one line per action when `--yes` ran (US-005), then the dry-run or result line. `--json` prints `WorkflowPromoteReport`.

`promote` ignores the sidecar's current `outcome` (including `abandoned`). The open items `promote` compares against come from `LoadedRun.openItems` (the run's recorded verdict), so a `ci` item written at publish time still needs a ruling even when the checks are green now. `waitForChecks(forge, prRef, opts: { cwd; timeoutMs; pollMs; signal?; expectedSha? }): Promise<CiWaitResult>` (`src/workflow/ci-wait.ts`) with `CiWaitResult = { outcome: "green" | "failed" | "pending" | "conflicting" | "no-checks" | "unavailable"; detail: string }`; a would-be green poll whose reported sha differs from `expectedSha` ends as `unavailable` with the mismatch as `detail`.

Failure handling: `promote`: outcome is not `draft`, no url, already ready, no forge -> exit 1; nothing written. `promote`: an open item has no ruling, or CI is not green on the pushed head -> exit 2; nothing written, even with `--yes`. `promote`: HEAD cannot be read -> exit 1 with `cannot read HEAD: <detail>`; nothing written. Invalid feature name, no workflow run, run not started -> exit 1 with `status`'s messages.

Create the shared draft-run test fixture `packages/nax/test/helpers/workflow-promote-fixture.ts` (a run directory with open item `B1`, a ruling sidecar, a stubbed forge reporting a draft PR whose body holds the `B1` checklist line, and `waitForChecks` returning `green`); US-004 and US-005 tests both import it. Tests stub `waitForChecks` rather than freeze the clock. Update the registration test in `workflow-status.test.ts` to expect exactly `["status", "record", "promote"]`. Extend the `### nax workflow` section of `docs/guides/cli-reference.md` with `promote`: flags, the two checks and the exit codes.

**Scope** — In: `WorkflowForgeDeps.waitForChecks`, `workflow-promote.ts`, registration, exports, fixture, docs. Out: the `tick`, `comment`, `ready` and `record` forge/sidecar writes behind `--yes` (US-005). Also out: waiting for CI (`--wait`/`--timeout`), promoting an already-ready PR, and adding a single-poll branch to `waitForChecks`.

**Interface**
```typescript
// cli/workflow-forge.ts
export interface WorkflowForgeDeps { forge: ForgeDeps; now: () => Date; waitForChecks: typeof waitForChecks }

// cli/workflow-promote.ts
export interface WorkflowPromoteOptions { dir: string; feature: string; yes: boolean; json: boolean }
export interface PromoteCheck { name: "items-ruled" | "ci-green"; passed: boolean; detail: string }
export interface PromoteAction { name: "tick" | "comment" | "ready" | "record"; status: "done" | "skipped" }
export interface WorkflowPromoteReport { feature: string; runId: string; url: string; dryRun: boolean; promoted: boolean; checks: readonly PromoteCheck[]; actions: readonly PromoteAction[] }
export async function workflowPromoteCommand(opts: WorkflowPromoteOptions, deps: WorkflowCliDeps, forgeDeps: WorkflowForgeDeps): Promise<number>;
```
acceptanceCriteria: `workflow promote -f auth --json -d <dir>` on a draft run with open item `B1`, a sidecar ruling `B1`, a PR the stubbed forge reports as a draft and `waitForChecks` returning `green`, exits 0 and prints one JSON object with `dryRun` true, `promoted` false and `checks` holding `items-ruled` and `ci-green` both `passed` true.
In that run the forge stub receives none of `gh pr edit`, `gh pr comment`, `gh pr ready`, `glab mr update` or `glab mr note create`.
With open items `B1` and `B2` and a sidecar ruling only `B1`, `promote` exits 2 and the `items-ruled` check has `passed` false and `detail` `no ruling recorded for B2`.
With open item `B1` and no sidecar in the run directory, the `items-ruled` check has `passed` false and `detail` `no decisions recorded; run nax workflow record`.

When `waitForChecks` returns `{ outcome: "pending", detail: "no CI result within 0ms" }`, `promote` exits 2 and the `ci-green` check has `passed` false and `detail` `ci pending: no CI result within 0ms`.
When `waitForChecks` returns outcome `no-checks`, `promote` exits 2 and `ci-green` has `passed` false.
When `waitForChecks` returns outcome `conflicting`, `promote` exits 2 and `ci-green` has `passed` false.

`promote` calls `waitForChecks` once, with the forge detected for `<dir>`, the record's `url` as the PR reference, `timeoutMs` 0 and `expectedSha` equal to the trimmed stdout of the stubbed forge's `git rev-parse HEAD` call.
When an open item is unruled and CI is `failed`, the report lists both checks with `passed` false (neither check hides the other).

When the stubbed forge's `pr view` call reports the PR as not a draft, `promote` exits 1 with error `PR is already ready: <url>` and the forge stub receives none of `gh pr edit`, `gh pr comment`, `gh pr ready`, `glab mr update` or `glab mr note create`.
On a run whose record `outcome` is `ready`, `promote` exits 1 with error `workflow for auth ended ready; only a draft can be promoted`.
On a run whose record has no `outcome`, `promote` exits 1 with error `workflow for auth ended not published; only a draft can be promoted`.
On a draft run whose record has no `url`, `promote` exits 1 with error `the workflow result has no PR url`.
When no forge is detected, `promote` exits 1 with error `no forge detected for <dir>`.
When the stubbed forge's `git rev-parse HEAD` call exits 128 with stderr `not a git repository`, `promote` exits 1 with error `cannot read HEAD: not a git repository`.
`workflow promote -f auth` without `--json` prints the lines `pass  items-ruled`, `pass  ci-green` and `ready to promote; rerun with --yes`.
`workflow promote -f auth` without `--json`, with CI pending, prints a line starting `FAIL  ci-green  ci pending`.
`workflow promote -f auth` where the run has no readable `result.json` exits 1 with error `no workflow result for feature auth`.
`workflow promote -f auth` where the newest `result.json` has no `featureWorkflow` exits 1 with an error starting `workflow for auth has not started its feature steps`.

When `waitForChecks` returns `{ outcome: "unavailable", detail: "checks report a1b2c3d4 but HEAD is e5f6a7b8" }`, `promote --yes` exits 2, `ci-green` has `passed` false and `detail` `ci unavailable: checks report a1b2c3d4 but HEAD is e5f6a7b8`, and the forge stub receives none of `gh pr edit`, `gh pr comment`, `gh pr ready`, `glab mr update` or `glab mr note create`.

`registerWorkflowCommand(new Command())` returns a group named `workflow` whose subcommand names equal `["status", "record", "promote"]`, and parsing `workflow promote -f auth --yes --json -d <dir>` calls `deps.exit` with the code `workflowPromoteCommand` returns for `{ dir: <dir>, feature: "auth", yes: true, json: true }`.

routing.reasoning: One new command file mirroring the already-built record command, composing existing helpers (loadRunVerdict, readPrState, waitForChecks) with no new abstractions; the validation order and exit codes are fully pinned by ACs.

suggestedCriteria: `workflow promote -f auth` with `waitForChecks` returning `failed` and `--json` prints one JSON object whose `ci-green` check has `detail` starting `ci failed:`.

modifiedFiles.reason: the registration test that US-002 changed to `["status", "record"]` now expects exactly `["status", "record", "promote"]`.

`WorkflowForgeDeps` gains `waitForChecks` and `_workflowForgeDeps` supplies the real one (the file is created by US-002).

userStories.title: nax workflow promote --yes: tick, comment, ready, record
acceptanceCriteria: `workflow promote -f auth --yes --json` issues forge commands in the order body edit, comment, ready; afterwards the sidecar on disk has `outcome` `promoted` and the record's `url`, the exit code is 0 and the report has `promoted` true.

In that run the body-edit command's body contains the PR body's `- [x] **B1**` line with the suffix for the sidecar's disposition of `B1`, and the comment command's text starts with `## Resolved before ready`.
When the PR body has no checklist line for any ruled id, `--yes` issues no body-edit command and the report marks the `tick` action `skipped`.

When the stubbed forge returns a changed body on its second `pr view` call (the first is the draft check, the second is the read immediately before the edit), the body written by the edit command contains that change.

`workflow promote -f auth --yes` with an unruled open item exits 2, the forge stub receives none of `gh pr edit`, `gh pr comment`, `gh pr ready`, `glab mr update` or `glab mr note create`, and the sidecar's bytes are unchanged.
`workflow promote -f auth --yes` with CI `failed` exits 2 and the forge stub receives none of `gh pr edit`, `gh pr comment`, `gh pr ready`, `glab mr update` or `glab mr note create`.

When the forge's comment command exits 1 with stderr `rate limited`, `promote --yes` exits 1 with error `promote stopped at comment: rate limited` and the forge stub receives no `gh pr ready` or `glab mr update --ready` command.

When the forge's ready command exits 1 with stderr `not mergeable`, `promote --yes` exits 1 with error `promote stopped at ready: not mergeable`, the body-edit and comment commands were already issued, and the sidecar's `outcome` is not `promoted`.
`workflow promote -f auth --yes` on a run with no sidecar and every check passing creates a sidecar with empty `decisions` whose `outcome` is `promoted` and whose `url` is the record's `url`.
`workflow promote -f auth --yes` with an existing sidecar whose `outcome` is `abandoned` rewrites that sidecar's `outcome` to `promoted`.

routing.reasoning: Extends one existing file with four sequential actions built from US-003's pure helpers and US-001's sidecar writer; stop-at-first-failure semantics are pinned by ACs, so no new abstractions are needed.

modifiedFiles.reason: extends the `nax workflow promote` text with the `--yes` actions.
`--yes` with both checks passing now runs the `tick`, `comment`, `ready` and `record` actions (the file is created by US-004).

analysis:
Phase 3 of #2569 (phases 1 `nax workflow status` #2574 and 2 `nax gates run` #2575 are merged). Adds `nax workflow record` and `nax workflow promote` to the `nax workflow` group in packages/nax.

Key existing code (all under packages/nax/src): `cli/workflow.ts` (registerWorkflowCommand, WorkflowCliDeps, _workflowCliDeps, file-local newestResult/fillStoryStates/reportFor/notStarted/noResult - these move to workflow/run-verdict.ts as loadRunVerdict with unchanged behaviour and error messages `no workflow result for feature <feature>` and `workflow for <feature> has not started its feature steps (run <runId>)`); `workflow/result.ts` (readResult, runDirsNewestFirst, storyStatesFrom, `_resultDeps = { mkdir, readdir, rename, stat }` file-system seam and temp-file-then-rename write pattern); `workflow/open-items.ts` (buildOpenItems, buildVerdict); `workflow/types.ts` (OpenItem at ~line 101, WorkflowFeatureRecord with outcome/url/head/reasons); `workflow/paths.ts` (workflowFeatureDir); `workflow/ci-wait.ts` (waitForChecks ~line 337, CiWaitResult); `workflow/pr-body.ts` (non-exported openItemLine renders `- [ ] **<id>** (<tags>) ...` with optional indented `  Suggestion:` / `  Advisor:` lines; gate items render `- [ ] **<id>** (gate) — ...`); `workflow/pr-body-safe.ts` (safeInline; currently imports escapeInline/escapeTableCell from the `@/finish` barrel); `forge/` (detectForge, viewArgv, defaultForgeDeps, ForgeDeps; barrel `@/forge`); `finish/pr/open.ts` (existing `gh pr ready` / `glab mr update --ready` argv); `utils/feature-name.ts` (validateFeatureName).

CRITICAL import-cycle constraint: the `@/workflow` barrel and `workflow/git.ts` load `step-context`, which imports `@/cli`. So new modules in `src/cli/` (workflow-forge.ts, workflow-record.ts, workflow-promote.ts) must import workflow leaves by relative path, import `src/cli/workflow.ts` only via `import type`, and must NOT value-import `workflow/git.ts` (`readHead`). HEAD is read via `forgeDeps.forge.run(["git","rev-parse","HEAD"], { cwd: dir })`. `workflow/pr-body-safe.ts` must switch its import from the `@/finish` barrel to the leaf `../finish/pr/escape` (no imports) so `workflow/promote.ts` can use safeInline without closing a cycle. `bun run check:import-cycles` must stay clean.

Dependency order: US-001 (decisions-sidecar data contract) -> US-002 (loadRunVerdict move, readPrState, WorkflowForgeDeps{forge,now}, `record`) and US-003 (pure tick/comment/argv text; also the pr-body-safe import fix) in parallel -> US-004 (promote validation + dry run; adds waitForChecks to WorkflowForgeDeps; creates shared test fixture test/helpers/workflow-promote-fixture.ts) -> US-005 (--yes writes: tick, comment, ready, record). US-004 performs no forge write even with --yes; US-005 adds the writes in the same PR.

Risks: (1) refactoring status's loader must keep output and exit codes byte-identical - test/unit/cli/workflow-status.test.ts covers it; its AC-15 subcommand-names assertion must be updated to ["status","record"] in US-002 and ["status","record","promote"] in US-004. (2) registerWorkflowCommand gains an optional third param forgeDeps; callers passing only deps keep working. (3) record tests build WorkflowForgeDeps by spreading _workflowForgeDeps and overriding forge/now so US-004's added waitForChecks field needs no test change. (4) Sidecar writes must be atomic (temp file in same directory, then rename); use _resultDeps-style injectable seam. (5) tickChecklist must compare ids as plain strings (B1 must not match **B10**; ids like `_run:ci` need no escaping) and modify only the first line of a matched `- [ ] **<id>**` entry. (6) promote tests stub waitForChecks rather than freeze the clock. (7) Docs: add `### nax workflow` section to docs/guides/cli-reference.md in US-002, extend in US-004 and US-005. (8) The decisions sidecar is git-ignored (`**/.nax/features/*/workflow/`) and left uncommitted. (9) Exit codes: record 0/1; promote 0 (all checks pass / promoted), 2 (a check failed), 1 (any error). --json prints exactly one JSON object; errors print {"error":"<message>"} on stdout, otherwise message goes to stderr via deps.logErr. Neither command calls the project trust gate (they run git/gh/glab only). Do not use mutation in new code; prefer many small files.
outOfScope: Promoting a PR that is already ready (the ready-audit case) is out of scope: `nax workflow promote` exits `1` with `PR is already ready: <url>` and writes nothing. The `## Verified after ready` evidence comment stays a manual step; `nax workflow record --outcome verified-ready` still records the audit.
`nax workflow promote` never waits for CI: it reads the checks once. There is no `--wait` or `--timeout` flag; a pending run exits `2` and the caller runs the command again.

`nax workflow promote` does not push, commit, rebase, or inspect the working tree. "Checks green on the pushed head" means the checks the forge reports are for the sha `git rev-parse HEAD` returns in `--dir`; GitHub reports that sha through `waitForChecks`, and where the forge reports none the comparison is skipped, as `waitForChecks` already does.
`nax workflow promote --yes` does not de-duplicate evidence comments: after a failure past the `comment` action, a re-run posts the comment again.
`nax workflow promote` edits no part of the PR body except the first line of matched checklist entries; refreshing or rewriting the body is not offered.
Converting a ready PR back to draft (`gh pr ready --undo`, `glab mr update --draft`) is out of scope for both commands.
`nax workflow record` validates the `id` and `kind` of an entry of kind `ci` or `minor` that names no open item only for shape; it does not check that the CI check or minor exists.
Neither command runs repository-controlled code (they run `git`, `gh` and `glab` only), so neither calls the project trust gate.

`nax workflow promote` can mark a head ready that was not the one it checked: `gh pr ready` and `glab mr update --ready` take no sha, so a push between the `ci-green` read and the `ready` action goes unverified.

`ci-green` is only as strong as `waitForChecks`: when the forge's auxiliary `gh pr view` read fails, `waitForChecks` skips both its head-sha binding and its conflict check, and `promote` does not add a second read.

`waitForChecks` with `timeoutMs: 0` and `pollMs: 0` returns after one poll because the deadline check sees the clock advance during the forge call; `promote` does not add a single-poll branch to `waitForChecks`, and its tests stub `waitForChecks` rather than freeze the clock.
`nax workflow record` validates the shape of a `fixed` entry's `sha` only; it does not check that the commit exists.
Concurrent `record` and `promote` calls on one run are not serialised: each write is atomic, but a read-merge-write can lose an entry another call wrote in between.
Neither command commits the decisions sidecar; the file is git-ignored and left where it is written.
Updating the nax-finish skill to call `nax workflow record` and `nax workflow promote` happens in nathapp-io/nax-toolkit-skills, outside this run.
Pipeline execution mode is frozen and out of scope; both commands read workflow-mode run directories only.
